name: Jean-Honoré Fragonard

summary.text: Jean-Honoré Fragonard was a French painter and printmaker whose late Rococo manner was distinguished by remarkable facility, exuberance, and hedonism.
summary.title: Jean-Honoré Fragonard

974414: Blind Man's Bluff is a painting by the French Rococo painter Jean-Honoré Fragonard, produced around 1750 in oil on canvas.
2629423: Young Girl Reading, or The Reader, is an 18th-century oil painting by Jean-Honoré Fragonard. It depicts an unidentified girl seated in profile, wearing a lemon yellow dress with white ruff collar and cuffs and purple ribbons, and reading from a small book held in her right hand.
2629559: The Swing, also known as The Happy Accidents of the Swing, is an 18th-century oil painting by Jean-Honoré Fragonard in the Wallace Collection in London. It is considered to be one of the masterpieces of the Rococo era, and is Fragonard's best-known work.
2886017: The Raised Chemise or The Shift Withdrawn is a small c.1770 oil-on-canvas painting by Jean-Honoré Fragonard, now in the Louvre in Paris, to which it was left by Dr Louis La Caze in 1869.
3190681: Jeroboam Sacrificing to Idols is a history painting by the French painter Jean-Honoré Fragonard, in oil on canvas.
3201472: Adoration of the Shepherds is an oil on canvas painting by Jean-Honoré Fragonard, from 1775. It was previously misattributed to François Boucher.
3211034: The Birth of Venus is an oil-on-canvas painting by the French Rococo painter Jean-Honoré Fragonard, produced between 1753 and 1755. It is held by the Musée Grobet-Labadié in Marseille.
3220204: The Stolen Kiss is an oil painting on canvas executed in 1787 and located in the Hermitage Museum, Saint Petersburg. It has been historically attributed to the French Rococo artist Jean-Honoré Fragonard (1732–1806).
3228069: The Bolt, also known as The Lock, is a galant scene painted by Jean-Honoré Fragonard in 1777. It is one of the most famous paintings by the painter.
3232204: The New Model is a c. 1770 oil-on-canvas painting by Jean-Honoré Fragonard, acquired by Édouard André before his marriage and now in the Musée Jacquemart-André.
3399523: The Fantastical Portraits or Fantasy Portraits are a series of portraits by the French painter Jean-Honoré Fragonard, mostly dating to 1769. It is said that each was executed in a single hour, from which they gained the Italian name fa' presto.
3815048: The Jean-Claude Richard, Abbot of Saint-Non, Dressed à l'Espagnole is a painting by Jean-Honoré Fragonard conserved at the National Art Museum of Catalonia, in Barcelona, from c. 1769.
Jean-Claude Richard, Abbot of Saint-Non, Dressed à l'Espagnole
5967115: The Music Lesson is an oil-on-canvas painting by the French artist Jean Honoré Fragonard, created c. 1770, now held in the Louvre, in Paris, to which it was donated by Hippolyte Walferdin in 1849.
8703547: The Visit to the Nursery is an oil-on-canvas painting by French artist Jean-Honoré Fragonard, created c. 1775, now held in the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C., which it entered in 1946 as part of the Samuel H. Kress collection.
12859945: The See-Saw is an oil-on-canvas painting by French Rococo artist Jean-Honoré Fragonard, created c.1750–1752 during the artist's early career. It is currently in the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum in Madrid.
19911872: The Woman With A Dog is an oil on canvas painting created in 1769 by Rococo artist Jean-Honoré Fragonard as part of his Figures de Fantaisie series.
19966728: Coresus Sacrificing Himself to Save Callirhoe is a large oil-on-canvas painting by the French Rococo artist Jean-Honoré Fragonard, created in 1765. The painting was exhibited at the Salon of 1765 and earned Fragonard entry into the Académie royale de peinture et de sculpture.
Coresus Sacrificing Himself to Save Callirhoe
26693141: Psyche Showing Her Sisters Her Gifts from Cupid is an oil painting by the French artist Jean-Honoré Fragonard, painted in 1753, in the National Gallery in London. Its dimensions are 168.3 by 192.4 cm.
Psyche Showing Her Sisters Her Gifts from Cupid
28801539: La Gimblette is one of the most famous paintings by the French painter Jean-Honoré Fragonard and one of the most famous Rococo paintings.
29855883: The Storm is an oil on canvas painting by Jean-Honoré Fragonard that hangs in the Louvre, in Paris. Painted during his time in Rome, it was inspired by the caravan pictures of Giovanni Benedetto Castiglione that were particularly admired in Paris.
61893530: The Little Park is a c.1763 landscape painting by the French artist Jean-Honoré Fragonard. It features a view of the gardens of the Villa d'Este in Tivoli near Rome.
83742682: Blind Man's Buff is an oil-on-canvas painting by Jean-Honoré Fragonard, produced ca. 1775–1780 after the artist's second journey to Italy in 1773–74. It is now in the Timken Museum of Art in San Diego, California.
88588236: The Musical Contest is a c.1755 genre painting by the French artist Jean-Honoré Fragonard. Rococo in style, it is part of the tradition of fête galante pictures popular in the eighteenth century.
107612614: The Palette Game is a c. 1761–1765 oil-on-canvas painting by Jean-Honoré Fragonard, showing an idyll with a happy company in a natural landscape dominated by ruins.
107612670: The See-Saw is an oil painting on canvas of c. 1761–1765 by Jean-Honoré Fragonard.
